promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The murder of which socialist deputy in 1924 provoked a major crisis for Mussolini's regime?
questions.explain: The kidnapping and murder of Giacomo Matteotti in June 1924, after he denounced Fascist violence, triggered the Matteotti Crisis.

questions.q: What was abolished by the National Assembly's decrees of 4-11 August 1789?
questions.explain: On the night of 4 August 1789 the Assembly abolished feudal privileges and seigneurial dues, dismantling the legal framework of the ancien regime.

questions.q: Which two leaders confronted each other during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
questions.explain: President Kennedy and Soviet leader Khrushchev faced off over missiles in Cuba in 1962.

questions.q: In which year was NATO founded?
questions.explain: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was established in April 1949.

questions.q: The Social Security Act, introducing federal old-age pensions, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Social Security Act of 1935 created old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.

questions.q: In which year did Gorbachev become Soviet leader?
questions.explain: Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary in March 1985, launching reform.

questions.q: The Wagner Act of 1935 is significant because it did what?
options: Guaranteed workers' rights to unionise and bargain collectively
questions.explain: The 1935 Wagner (National Labor Relations) Act protected the right of workers to organise and bargain collectively.

questions.q: In which year did Fascist Italy invade Abyssinia (Ethiopia)?
questions.explain: Italy invaded Abyssinia in October 1935, completing its conquest in 1936 and provoking League of Nations sanctions.

questions.q: In which year did the assassination of Abraham Lincoln take place, just days after Lee's surrender at Appomattox?
questions.explain: Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth on 14 April 1865 and died the following day, shortly after the Civil War ended.

questions.q: Which arms-limitation treaty was signed in 1972?
questions.explain: SALT I, signed in 1972, limited strategic nuclear arms and capped ABM systems.

questions.q: The Montgomery Bus Boycott, sparked by Rosa Parks's arrest, began in which year?
questions.explain: The boycott began in December 1955 after Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat.

questions.q: In which year was the Soviet Union formally dissolved?
questions.explain: The USSR was officially dissolved in December 1991, ending the Cold War.

questions.q: Which factor is most commonly cited as intensifying the witch craze in the period of religious conflict?
options: Confessional rivalry between Protestants and Catholics after the Reformation
questions.explain: Reformation-era confessional anxiety and rivalry between Protestants and Catholics heightened fears of diabolical conspiracy.

questions.q: In which year was Louis XVI executed by guillotine?
questions.explain: Convicted of treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined on 21 January 1793.

questions.q: In which year did Italy join the First World War, declaring war on Austria-Hungary?
questions.explain: Italy entered the war on the Entente side in May 1915 after the secret Treaty of London promised territorial gains.

questions.q: At which 1815 battle was Napoleon finally defeated, ending his Hundred Days?
questions.explain: Napoleon was decisively defeated at Waterloo on 18 June 1815 by Wellington and Blucher, leading to his exile to St Helena.

questions.q: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, bringing the USA into the Second World War, took place on which date?
questions.explain: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, prompting the US declaration of war.

questions.q: The 1917 Italian military catastrophe against Austro-German forces is known as the Battle of which place?
questions.explain: At Caporetto in October-November 1917 the Italian army suffered a devastating defeat, deepening post-war disillusionment.

questions.q: The Selma to Montgomery marches, which helped galvanise support for voting rights, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Selma marches of March 1965 dramatised the struggle for the vote in the South.

questions.q: Who had replaced Roosevelt as US President by the Potsdam Conference?
questions.explain: Roosevelt died in April 1945, so Harry Truman represented the US at Potsdam.

questions.q: The Black Panther Party, advocating self-defence and black empowerment, was founded in 1966 in which city?
questions.explain: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale founded the Black Panther Party in Oakland, California, in 1966.

questions.q: The GI Bill of 1944 chiefly provided what for returning servicemen?
options: Education funding, loans and unemployment pay
questions.explain: The 1944 Servicemen's Readjustment Act (GI Bill) funded veterans' education, home loans and unemployment benefits.

questions.q: The radical phase of the Revolution known as the Terror was dominated by which committee?
questions.explain: The Committee of Public Safety, with Robespierre prominent, directed the Terror of 1793-94 through revolutionary tribunals and emergency powers.

questions.q: On what date did the Parisian crowd storm the Bastille?
questions.explain: The fortress-prison of the Bastille fell to the Parisian crowd on 14 July 1789, a symbolic blow against royal despotism.

questions.q: What document, proclaiming universal natural rights, did the National Assembly adopt in August 1789?
options: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
questions.explain: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted on 26 August 1789, asserting liberty, equality and popular sovereignty.

questions.q: The Civil Rights Act of 1968 is best known for prohibiting discrimination in which area?
questions.explain: The 1968 Civil Rights (Fair Housing) Act outlawed discrimination in the sale and rental of housing.

questions.q: President Lyndon B. Johnson's domestic reform programme of the mid-1960s was known as what?
questions.explain: Johnson's 'Great Society' programme aimed to end poverty and racial injustice, creating Medicare and Medicaid in 1965.

questions.q: At which 1187 battle did Saladin annihilate the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Hattin (4 July 1187) Saladin destroyed the Frankish field army, leaving the kingdom defenceless.

questions.q: Which five-man executive governed France from 1795 until Napoleon's coup?
questions.explain: The Directory, a five-member executive established under the Constitution of 1795, governed France until the coup of Brumaire in 1799.

questions.q: In which year did the USSR first test an atomic bomb, ending the US monopoly?
questions.explain: The Soviet Union detonated its first atomic bomb in 1949.
